head: bd556e58ce91797a3b0b1abf11dfd9f93cae07ec
summary:
Attempt 2 applies the fix accepted for m1 (O-015), and it works. In StartupHook.cs:121-133, Act now has its own try/catch inside the Invoke callback. On an exception it logs 'rethrown' and hands the exception back to the dispatcher through ExceptionDispatchInfo and BeginInvoke(Send), so the app's handler sees it. `acted = true` comes after that try/catch. In WindowCases.ps1:295-303, CheckActed now also fails when a 'refused' line follows the 'acted' line. WindowMutants.ps1 adds two mutants. CancelThrows makes OnCancel throw; HookFailsAfterActing makes the hook throw after it presses Stop. Its one-FAIL match became an ordered list of expected FAIL lines, plus optional Expect lines the run must show.

What I ran against this tree:
- Core tests: 120/120.
- C-006, C-012 and O-016: each passed. The hook acted at 527, 641 and 658 ms; the new 'the hook did not fail after it acted' check passed in all three.
- WindowMutants -Mutant All: all 8 passed. CancelThrows logged 'rethrown mode=stop ...', the app exited 70, and C-006 failed on exactly 'exit code' and 'a report was written'. That is the reverse of the exit 0 and Finished report I measured before the fix. HookFailsAfterActing failed C-006 only on the new check. The six mutants from attempt 1 still fail as planted under the new ordered-match logic.
- Fitness (rebuilt): 20 rules hold. No DllImport, Shutdown, Exit or ExitCode appears in the hook.

I also ran one probe of my own: OnClosing mutated to throw once, then O-016. It showed that part of my own m1 claim was wrong. A fault in OnClosing never reaches the hook's catch, either now or at 105f1a4. Window.Close() goes through WM_CLOSE and the window procedure, and WPF hands that exception straight to App.DispatcherUnhandledException: exit 70, and no 'rethrown' line. So only stop mode needed the fix, and only stop mode is proved by a mutant. I have put this in drift, not in findings. No scratch copies or app processes were left behind, and git status shows only the engine's own files.

obligations.evidence: Test-C006 main step (tests/window/WindowCases.ps1), re-run on this tree: 'acted mode=stop ... ms=527', the new after-acted check passed, then exit 0, report, Cancelled and the Stopped title. PASSED.
CheckActed still returns early when no 'acted' line exists (WindowCases.ps1:300). Re-run StopDisabled: the scan ended before the hook could act, and C-006 failed only on 'the hook acted'.
WindowMutants.ps1 StopDisabled, re-run under the new ordered match: C-006 failed on /the hook acted/ and nothing else.
WindowMutants.ps1 StopCollapsed, re-run: C-006 failed on /the hook acted/ and nothing else.
No-scan step of Test-C006, re-run: 'waiting found=True enabled=True visible=False', then 'refused mode=stop ... within 20 s', with no 'acted' line.
Test-C012 re-run: 'acted mode=throw ... ms=641', no 'refused' after it, exit 70 (0x00000046), stale report gone, no .tmp.
WindowMutants.ps1 NoCrashHandler re-run: C-012 failed only on the exit code, actual -532462766 (0xE0434352).
Test-O016 re-run: 'acted mode=close ... ms=658', exit 70, stale report gone, no .tmp.
WindowMutants.ps1 NoExitRule re-run: O-016 failed only on the exit code, actual 0 (0x00000000).
Invoke-WithHook is unchanged: the variables are set in try and removed with Remove-Item Env: in finally. The cleanup step in Test-C006 re-ran ok for all three variables.

The inert-host and control steps of Test-C006 re-ran ok. The ProcessPath check in StartupHook.Initialize (:50-52) is unchanged. My attempt-1 probe showed the empty-log assertion fails when that check is removed.

WindowMutants.ps1 HookCompileError (CS1029) and HookLocked (MSB3021/3027) re-ran: each exits 1, stops at Update-Hook, and leaves the earlier dll unchanged. Attempt-1 probe: a real app holding the dll gives the same MSB3027.

NoCrashHandler (0xE0434352) and NoExitRule (exit 0) still make their cases fail against the hook as it now stands. The rethrow only hands back an exception the app's own handler raised, and the hook still never exits, shuts down or sets an exit code: the Fitness rule 'the hook never produces the outcome under test' holds.

The Pressable gate (StartupHook.cs:68) and the check-then-act inside one Invoke callback are unchanged. StopDisabled and StopCollapsed re-ran and fail C-006 on 'the hook acted'; the no-scan step refuses.

StartupHook.cs:121-133 wraps Act in try/catch, logs 'rethrown mode=<m> reason=...', and re-posts the exception with ExceptionDispatchInfo.Capture(e) and Dispatcher.BeginInvoke(DispatcherPriority.Send, new Action(fault.Throw)). WindowCases.ps1:299-302 fails CheckActed on any 'refused' after 'acted'. Measured: CancelThrows gives 'rethrown mode=stop reason=InvalidOperationException: mutant: OnCancel threw', app exit 70, and C-006 fails on exactly 'exit code' and 'a report was written'. HookFailsAfterActing fails C-006 only on 'the hook did not fail after it acted'.

cases.evidence: Test-C006 main step on the 30,150-folder New-LargeTree, re-run: the hook acted at 527 ms mid-scan; the ending was Stopped.
Exercised through StopDisabled and StopCollapsed: the hook never acts and the scan runs to its end. CheckActed's early return makes C-006 fail once, on 'the hook acted'. Re-run passed.
WindowMutants.ps1 StopDisabled edits StartScan in a scratch copy so the button is disabled. Re-run: C-006 failed on that line only.
WindowMutants.ps1 StopCollapsed collapses the button in a scratch copy. Re-run: C-006 failed on that line only.
The no-scan step of Test-C006 opens the window with no root: the button is enabled but hidden. Re-run: 'waiting ... visible=False' and a refusal, with no 'acted' line.
Test-C012: stale report planted, and mode throw posts an exception through BeginInvoke mid-scan. Re-run: exit 70, report gone.
WindowMutants.ps1 NoCrashHandler, re-run: C-012 failed only on 0xE0434352.

Test-O016: stale report planted, and Close() is called while Stop is pressable. Re-run: exit 70, no report. See drift: a fault in OnClosing also gives 70 and no report, and O-016 cannot tell the two apart.
WindowMutants.ps1 NoExitRule, re-run: O-016 failed only on exit 0.
Test-C006's cleanup step throws inside Invoke-WithHook, then checks that all three variables are removed. Re-run ok.
Test-C006 runs pwsh 7 under the hook with a control step first. Re-run ok. In attempt 1 I showed this step fails when the ProcessPath check is removed.
HookCompileError and HookLocked, re-run: Update-Hook exits 1 with the build error and the old dll is left untouched. In attempt 1 I confirmed that a real app holding the dll fails the same way.
No test sets an unknown mode. The design marked this immaterial; the branch at StartupHook.Run :75-79 is unchanged.
No test uses a relative path or one containing ';'. The design marked this immaterial, and $HookDll is still absolute.

drift: Correction to my own m1 from attempt 1. Its O-016 half was wrong: 'A throwing OnClosing would fail O-016 under the hook'. I measured OnClosing mutated to throw once. Window.Close() runs through WM_CLOSE and the window procedure, and WPF hands that exception straight to App.DispatcherUnhandledException. The hook's catch never sees it: no 'rethrown' line, exit 70, no report, O-016 PASSED. The same would have happened at 105f1a4. So the new catch matters only for stop mode, which the CancelThrows mutant covers. The comment at StartupHook.cs:127-129 ('The app's own handler threw (OnCancel for stop, OnClosing for close)') is wrong about OnClosing. The behaviour is right, but the tree slice should not copy that comment.

O-016 cannot tell 'the window closed and the Exit rule turned exit 0 into 70' apart from 'the app faulted while closing and the crash handler exited 70'. Both give exit 70 and no report. Measured with an OnClosing that throws: O-016 passes. The report-mode black-box contract holds either way, and this was already true before this attempt, so I have not filed it. The only proof that the Exit rule is what produces the 70 remains the NoExitRule mutant.

Contract change carried by the accepted O-015 fix. The design's error_cases said 'Any exception in the hook: caught and logged, never fatal.' Now an exception raised inside Act is logged as 'rethrown' and handed back to the app, which ends the process when the app has no handler. The builder declared the new log-line kind but not this change to the 'never fatal' clause. Nothing the hook's own code does inside Act can realistically throw (throw mode's BeginInvoke and a Close() while pressable), so in practice this carries only the app's own faults.
